representation_note: 3D model drawn from published catalog and literature values, not measured by SPHEREx unless a fact says 'seen by SPHEREx' (each fact shows its source) - not an image. What no source gives is not drawn: an unknown temperature is drawn grey and an unknown size at a fixed marker size, not to scale. Sizes and distances may be exaggerated for visibility.

notes: Values checked on 2026-11-14 against the NASA Exoplanet Archive, SIMBAD (CfA mirror), Gaia DR3, VizieR and the cited papers (tasks/WS7-3d-systems.md, WS7-2). Facts still marked 'unverified' are estimates no source states. The 'seen by SPHEREx' facts were copied from the validation records (docs/validation/; AI analysis with an independent second analysis, human review pending), not from that catalog cross-check.

The pulsation is drawn as a brightness change only: the radius is drawn constant, because its size change is not measured. It runs on two clocks. Free-running: the brightness animation is a sine wave at the GCVS period (245.6 d) spanning the V-band range, with an arbitrary phase (no epoch): it is not a prediction for a real date. Dataset time: R Dra is drawn at the phase predicted by the AAVSO VSX ephemeris (epoch of maximum HJD 2457370.00, P = 246.12 d) on an asymmetric curve that rises in 45 % of the cycle, with the timing band of the WS7 table frontend/src/three/ephemerides.ts (from the O−C of observed maxima against that ephemeris). Both are catalog V-band drawings, not measured by SPHEREx: real Mira cycles change from cycle to cycle, and the amplitude is much smaller in the infrared: offline measurements on the SPHEREx FITS files give 0.5–1.3 mag peak-to-peak at 0.74–5.0 µm and a ~260-day cycle in 2025–2026 (docs/validation/r-draconis.md). The animation is not that light curve, and the SPHEREx images in this app do not show it. The R Draconis field page shows the precomputed SPHEREx light curve (WS3/WS4 product) in live API mode.
Radial velocity −132.8 km/s from SIMBAD (Wilson 1953); optical lines of a Mira move with the pulsation.

Not measured, so not drawn (shown as unknown): R Draconis: temperature (it changes with the pulsation: the literature gives ~2000–3300 K (van Belle et al. 2002; McDonald et al. 2012), and one drawn value would be a pick inside that range; WS3 object context: Gaia DR3 has no temperature for this source; no temperature fit to the SPHEREx spectrum yet, WS3 V18), radius (published sizes depend on the assumed distance and the pulsation phase; no measured angular diameter is adopted here; WS3 object context: Gaia DR3 FLAME gives no radius for this source; no radius from the SPHEREx flux and the distance yet, WS7-8), mass (no dynamical mass is published for R Dra; WS3 object context: Gaia DR3 FLAME gives no mass for this source).
